questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the university had courses in english and that they seemed interesting.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the Erasmus University of Rotterdam was really helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a introduction day, with a guide around campus. We were also divided into small group with two mentors connected to each group.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It wasn't easy and Rotterdam is super expensive. I ended up living in a great location, but the housing itself wasn't good. I would recommend getting the housing on campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's probably gonna be more expensive. I found my housing through campus, but a company that they had a deal with. This doesn't mean it's as good as the one's on campus. But when I had trouble with my housing it has been possible to contact the university and ask for help too, which has been nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not a lot, very expensive and not even clean.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It has been easy and the university was very helpful. You could always write the exchange office with questions and they would help you.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could write or call the exchange office and if you had forgotten something in the process they would write you and remind you.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful, got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be ready when registration opens, I got all my classes because I was fast.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I would say I haven't struggled with the level of the courses but rather the fact that it's a different system and another structure for the courses. I had classes that were 1st year classes even though I'm a third year student. This I think is annoying hasn't been mentioned to me, but the classes has been interesting because they are so different from what I would have back home.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I think the styl of teaching has been a little shallow and hectic. Because of the block-structure nothing really went in depth, which has been annoying.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Cinema and Society
Future Scenarios for the Cultural Sector
Sociology, Culture and Modernity
Art, Culture and Media
Feeling Orange

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Art, Culture and Media has been interesting and different for me.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: At my housing they have charged a few unexpected payments, but this was immediatly cancelled with help from the university.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The rent here has been the most expensive thing.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There has been so many events that you could participate in. Open-air movie nights, painting workshops and trip to different places.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going on some of the trips that they plan to museums and so, it's usually cheaper through the university.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Holland is so small so it's easy to visit other cities with the train. If you get a personal OV-chipcard with a subscription then it's also affordable. You can also get a Rotterdam pass and get into the museums for free.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, it's similar to danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: This can be difficult since there is so many exchange students. I have made some friends in class, but it is also an experience to meet people from all over the world.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Can't think of any important ones.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Netherlands is a very relaxed country like Denmark. The mentality isn't that different.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Expect to use a lot of money, especially on housing. 
It's okay to talk to mainly other exchange students.
And lastly, go on day-trips to other cities.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Registrate for classes just when it opens, that was how I got the ones I wanted.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing a different kind of university and meeting people from all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Housing.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
